# Results — Study 12 (Paper-Prophet) on the SPY tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The article's ARIMA(1,0,1)+GARCH(1,1)
stack, ported faithfully and run **cold** (refit every day) walk-forward over cached daily SPY
(split-only). As-of **2026-06-01**; sample **8,391** closes 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-01; fingerprint
**`0c5568d20239`**. Returns in percent (the article's scale).*

## Stationarity — the one thing the article gets right
```
ADF p-value, price levels : 1.000   (> 0.05 -> unit root, do NOT model)
ADF p-value, log-returns  : 0.0000   (< 0.05 -> stationary, model THIS)
```
Prices have a unit root; returns don't. We model returns, as the article correctly insists.

## Signal — is the ARIMA direction better than a coin?
```
walk-forward hit-rate     : 51.98%   (n = 8,091 graded days)
directional edge / day    : +1.035 bp   (HAC t = +0.85)
```
The one-step direction is a **coin flip**: hit-rate ≈ 50%, HAC t well inside ±2.

## The Sharpe is the sizing, not the forecast
```
Sharpe — full stack (sign x size)        : +0.174
Sharpe — constant-long x same GARCH size : +0.527   (pure vol-targeting)
Sharpe — forecast, flat size (sign only) : +0.138
Sharpe — plain buy & hold                : +0.454
vol-targeting reproduces                 : 302% of the stack Sharpe
ARIMA increment (stack - vol-targeting)  : -0.352  (boot CI [-0.74, +0.07], 95% neg)
```

## Alpha vs (managed) beta
```
stack ~ a + b * buy&hold   : beta = 0.163, alpha = +0.0040%/day, R2 = 0.050
stack ~ a + b * vol-managed : beta = 0.310, alpha = +0.0006%/day, R2 = 0.096
```
Against the vol-managed-SPY factor the stack's alpha collapses — it *is* the vol-targeting factor.

## "Win every single trade"?
```
per-day win rate          : 51.98%   (n_active = 8,091)
```
A coin flip. The headline is mathematically impossible and empirically ~50%.
